newsitem.title: VIETNAM: World Bank to help Hanoi beat traffic chaos.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to help Hanoi beat traffic chaos.

text.p: A World Bank plan to upgrade Hanoi's road network and restore order to its treacherous streets has been submitted to the government, the official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said on Saturday.

VNA said most of the $24.8 million earmarked for the four-year project would be spent on improving four arterial roads, the shabby but bustling old quarter and the elegant northwestern district built by Vietnam's former French colonial masters.
Under the plan, traffic control at 212 of the capital's road intersections would be improved and 43.4 km (27.1 miles) of road would be repaired.
Some $2.8 million of the funding would help provide traffic police with modern equipment and improve the efficiency of the Urban Transport Control department.
More than 2,500 people were killed in road accidents in Vietnam in the first six months of this year -- this in a country where the majority still ride bicycles.
Swarms of motorbikes and, increasingly, cars have arrived on the nation's chaotic and often potholed streets since economic and social reforms were launched in the late 1980s.
Small motorbikes are the most popular form of transport in the cities, but traffic rules are lax and crash helmets are considered expensive and unfashionable.
VNA did not say whether the government would approve the project. However, aid projects are rarely turned down.
